text:
The fed funds rate is 1.70%, the 2-year yield 2.42% and the 10-year 2.84%, with unemployment at 3.9%. That combination points to mid-2018. The fed funds rate was about 1.70% in April and May 2018 (the effective rate was 1.70% in April and 1.70% in May, rising to 1.91% in June).

The 10-year yield was about 2.84% at the end of May 2018, and the 2-year was about 2.40%. Unemployment was 3.9% in April and 3.8% in May 2018. The latest value of 3.9% suggests either April or May data, and a 3-month change of -0.2 fits April, when unemployment was 3.9% against 4.1% in January.

US equities returned +2.2% over 1m, and May 2018 S&P was +2.4%, which fits May. The 10-year Treasury 1m return of +1.1% also fits May, when yields fell from 3.0% to 2.84%. The VIX at 14.94 fits end of May. CPI at 2.43% YoY in April fits as the latest published value at the end of May.

So the snapshot describes May 2018.
